props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — one event per accepted transition, with per-series PR subjects

text.insert: Every accepted revision of a durable state object is produced by exactly one event: event_type names the transition semantically, and StateEnvelope.caused_by_event_id is therefore never null after creation. The status tables in this feature double as the transition catalog — each table row's entry and exit transitions define events mechanically, so per-status events are not separately enumerated in the event table; the table below lists the coordination, lifecycle, and recovery events whose payloads need explicit facts. Every workflow has an explicit recovery event: run.recovered, sync.recovered, and pr.campaign_recovered. Event topology follows state topology: the campaign is the containing PR workflow, but each PR series is its own event subject — feedback, revision, approval, merge, and close events carry subject_id of the individual series, with correlation_id grouping them under the campaign — so a consumer can process one PR's stream in isolation. Explicitly desired future relaxation: per-series triggers that react to these streams and handle routine review changes more out-of-loop; v1 keeps fixer execution operator-gated per the PR-phase decision.
